subject: ForgePoint integration - SOW / procurement clarifications
messages:
From: Jane Su <jane.su@forgepoint.io>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom@forgepoint.io>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft SOW and procurement checklist for Redwood integration

Hi Monica,

Great to connect last week — attaching the first-draft SOW (ForgePoint_SOW_v1.1.docx) and our standard procurement checklist. We scoped the work as: connector development (2 devs, 6 weeks), joint onboarding, and a 6-month success engagement.

A few initial notes from procurement that may affect timing:
- We need confirmation on data residency + whether Redwood will accept our standard DPA (attached).
- Standard ForgePoint terms include a 60-day invoice payment term — will that work?
- Insurance: we require 1M/3M by default; can Redwood meet that?

If you can share Redwoods' preferred SOW changes and any required MSA/DPA redlines, we can loop legal on our side. If easier, we can set a 30-minute procurement sync tomorrow.

Attachments: ForgePoint_SOW_v1.1.docx; Security_Questionnaire_Fill.pdf

Thanks,
Jane Su
Head of Partnerships | ForgePoint Analytics
jane.su@forgepoint.io
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Jane Su <jane.su@forgepoint.io>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW and procurement checklist for Redwood integration

Hi Jane — thanks for the SOW and the checklist. Quick read-through and a few high-level procurement/legal points from our side before we engage legal:

1) Data residency & data handling
- Redwood can host connector operations in us-west (NA) or eu-west (EU) regions depending on the customer. For this engagement we need to clarify which region(s) ForgePoint requires. If EU is required, we'll need to confirm a EU-hosted variant and add the relevant addendum to the SOW.

2) DPA and security
- We cannot sign a substitute DPA without walking through a few clauses: subprocessors, data deletion timelines, and audit rights. Please send the DPA you referenced (we got the questionnaire but not the DPA PDF).

3) Payment terms
- 30 days is our standard for new partner integrations. 60 days is longer than our typical and will require FP leadership approval.

4) Insurance and indemnity
- Redwood typically carries 1M/3M and can provide evidence, but indemnity caps are contract-specific. We will ask legal to propose a mutual cap tied to the SOW fees (standard practice).

5) Termination and liabilities for multitenant connectors
- We need the SOW to be explicit around support windows, rollback responsibilities, and any customer-facing SLA. Please confirm if ForgePoint expects Redwood to own the connector in perpetuity or hand over code to ForgePoint at the end of the engagement.

Next steps I propose:
- Please share the full DPA and your preferred MSA redline.
- We'll circulate a short redline summary from Redwood's side (target end of day 07/08) and propose a 30-min procurement/legal sync for 07/09 or 07/10.

Linking our internal docs and a sandbox contract folder for both teams: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFP_SOW

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Jane Su <jane.su@forgepoint.io>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom@forgepoint.io>, procurement@forgepoint.io
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft SOW and procurement checklist for Redwood integration

Monica — appreciate the quick reply and helpful list. Attaching a slightly updated SOW (ForgePoint_SOW_v1.2-redline.docx) that:
- clarifies the handoff model (we had assumed ForgePoint takes ownership of the connector repo after delivery),
- adds a short SLA for connector uptime while ForgePoint manages day-to-day,
- keeps invoice terms at Net60 in our initial draft.

Attached also is the DPA PDF you requested. A couple of notes:
- We're comfortable discussing a short-term 60-day payment term for this first project if you can move to Net30 thereafter.
- For indemnity, our legal asks for a mutual cap of fees or liability except in cases of gross negligence.

Can we do a 30-min call Thursday 07/09 at 10:00 PT to run through the DPA carveouts and the insurance ask? Our procurement lead (procurement@forgepoint.io) will join.

Attachments: ForgePoint_SOW_v1.2-redline.docx; ForgePoint_DPA_v1.pdf

--
Jane Su
Head of Partnerships | ForgePoint Analytics

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW and procurement checklist for Redwood integration

Looping in a quick internal action list after Jane's update:

- Monica: push back on Net60 for ongoing billing — we can offer Net60 for the project milestone but require Net30 for future invoices. Confirm this in the redline summary.
- Vanessa: ask Legal to prioritize the DPA review — key items: subprocessors list, deletion SLA (30 days), and audit scope. If ForgePoint insists on unlimited audit rights, we should propose a scoped audit with notice.
- Monica + Vanessa: insurance — confirm current certificates (we already carry 1M/3M). If their ask is higher, get Legal to propose alternative mitigations (holdback, escrow).
- Schedule: confirm the 07/09 10:00 PT call and invite Legal and Procurement on Redwood side (Vanessa for legal).

On the call, keep the ask tight: data residency requirement, DPA carveouts, payment term, and IP/ownership of the connector. If we see significant MSA redlines, escalate to me before committing to terms.

Thanks — Vivek
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
